title: Weighted Memory Tree: Remembering What Matters for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

analysis.tldr: Weighted Memory Tree makes active-retention priority a stage before retrieval: a task tree scores, decays, folds, and suppresses branches before selected state reaches the actor. GAIA gains support the package, not any individual weighting or decay rule.
analysis.problem: Linear action history grows with task length and gives the actor little control over which subtask state remains active.
analysis.core_idea: Represent task, subtask, and action state as a tree; combine event importance, decay, branch priority, folding, and suppression to assemble a compact prompt for the next action.

memory_design.write: Task, subtask, action, observation, and event nodes are appended during one agent run.
memory_design.organize: The hierarchy carries weights, decay, and branch state; low-priority branches can be folded or suppressed from active context.
memory_design.read: A selected tree view is serialized into the later prompt and changes subsequent GAIA actions.
memory_design.update_forget: Scores and active visibility evolve, but records are not durably deleted; this is active-context retention rather than demonstrated long-term forgetting.

compared_to: The same GAIA agent with linear history
Tree plus selection plus summary package ablations
A token-matched flat priority queue and isolated decay/folding controls are missing
analysis.evidence: Across three models on GAIA-Text, the full package averages +9.97 percentage points over linear history while reducing prompt tokens 32.8%. The unweighted tree can be worse, and component effects vary by model and task, so only the combined active-retention package is supported.
analysis.why_it_matters: Before asking which memory to retrieve, an agent may need an explicit policy for which live task branches deserve scarce context.
limitations: No cross-session or cross-task persistence is tested, and active suppression is not durable forgetting.
No component has a fully matched factorial control; gains are model- and task-dependent without uncertainty estimates.
The study reports 6,132 executions, 2.391B prompt tokens, and eight RTX 6000 GPUs, but not GPU-hours, wall time, dollars, storage, or energy.
